White students made up 49.6% of Dinwiddie County's student body in 2025-26
A. L. Pullen
There were 2,000 white students enrolled in Dinwiddie County schools in the 2025-26 school year, 3.6% fewer than the previous year, according to the Virginia Department of Education.
Data showed that 4,036 students were enrolled in Dinwiddie County schools in the 2025-26 school year. Of those, white students comprised 49.6% of the student body, making them the most represented ethnicity in the county.
Among the seven schools in the county, Dinwiddie High School had the highest number of white students enrolled in the 2025-26 school year, with 584 students.
Virginia public schools have an average student-to-teacher ratio of 14:1, compared with the national average of 15:1, according to Public School Review. Minority students, primarily Hispanic and Black, make up 56% of the enrollment, while white students account for 44%.

| Southside Elementary School | 145 | 419 | 34.6% |
| Sunnyside Elementary School | 166 | 280 | 59.3% |
